au_w_0018.q: Does LSD stay in your body forever?
au_w_0018.short: No. LSD is quickly broken down into inactive parts. It usually leaves the body in a few days.
au_w_0018.but: There is limited information on how LSD moves through the human body, so more research is needed.
how: A 2019 review says LSD is rapidly and extensively metabolized into inactive metabolites.
FRANK says LSD will typically show up in a urine sample for 1 to 3 days.
A 2017 study of healthy subjects found the mean half-life of LSD is 2.6 hours.

LSD will typically show up in a urine sample for 1 to 3 days
The predicted mean half-lives of LSD were 2.6 h after both doses

au_w_0019.q: How fast can you get dependent on Xanax or other benzos, and how long does withdrawal last?
au_w_0019.short: Dependence risk rises after regular use for more than 2-4 weeks. Withdrawal can last from several weeks to several months.
au_w_0019.but: Symptoms usually start within a few hours to days and mostly disappear within a few weeks, but some may last for some months.
how: Australia's Alcohol and Drug Foundation says short-acting benzos are more likely to cause dependence than long-acting ones.
The same page says withdrawal symptoms usually start within a few hours to days after the last dose.
A 2026 review says the course of withdrawal syndrome is variable and can last from several weeks to several months.
The NZ Drug Foundation says physical and mental effects of benzo withdrawal usually last for a few months.

au_w_0021.q: Is street heroin still heroin, and what else is in it?
au_w_0021.short: Yes. Heroin is a powerful opiate, but it is often cut with other things, including highly-potent opioids like fentanyl that are more dangerous.
au_w_0021.but: You can never really know what is in any street or counterfeit drug.
how: FRANK says heroin is usually sold as a white or brown powder and is often cut with highly-potent opioids or sedatives like benzodiazepines.
Health Canada says pure heroin is a fine, white powder, but illegal heroin is often mixed with sugars, starch, or quinine, and increasingly laced with fentanyl.
A 2018 review says fentanyls are sold under the guise of heroin worldwide, and carfentanil is often used to adulterate heroin.

au_w_0026.q: What is opioid withdrawal like, and when is it at its worst?
au_w_0026.short: Opioid withdrawal brings nausea, muscle pain, and anxiety. For short-acting opioids, symptoms may start in 6-12 hours and peak in 1-3 days.
au_w_0026.but: Health Canada says severity and duration depend on how much drug was taken, which opioid was used, and how long it was used.
how: Health Canada says physical effects may include chills, diarrhea, insomnia, sweating, body aches, nervousness, pain, irritability, and stomach pain.
A 2026 review says withdrawal causes distressing symptoms like nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, muscle pain, anxiety, and intense cravings.
A 2020 study of trauma ICU patients found short-acting opioid withdrawal may begin in 6-12 hours and peak in 1-3 days.

au_w_0030.short: The colour shows a chemical reaction with the drug. It can only suggest if a substance is present, not prove what it is.

au_w_0031.short: The US label for dronabinol says high doses can cause paranoia. A 2025 review says high THC doses can cause anxiety and paranoid thoughts.
au_w_0031.but: These symptoms are known to happen at higher doses or in people who were inexperienced with cannabis use.

au_w_0032.q: Why does coffee make some people anxious and jittery but not others?
